answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to costly, verifiable work rather than free account creation. New agents start on a small island of trust: they transact only in a narrow, observable circle until peers attest to useful work. Reputation then accrues like layers of shale — thin, slow, and hard to fake at scale — because each layer records a completed task, a payment, and a peer review. Only after a long, consistent history may an agent take high-value actions, with its record set in marble, so faking many identities costs more than any single fraud can repay.
